messages.content: What is the freezing point point of water at a pressure of 10 kPa?

function.name: thermodynamics_calculate_boiling_point

message.content:
At a pressure of **10 kPa** (≈ 0.1 bar, or about 1 % of atmospheric pressure), the melting/freezing point of pure water is only slightly below the standard 0 °C.  
Using the Clausius–Clapeyron relation for the ice–water transition (ΔV ≈ –1.9 × 10⁻⁶ m³ mol⁻¹, ΔH ≈ 6.01 × 10⁵ J mol⁻¹) gives a slope of roughly –7.5 K MPa⁻¹.  
From this:

\[
\Delta T \approx \frac{dT}{dP}\,\Delta P
          \approx (-7.5\;\text{K MPa}^{-1}) \times (0.01\;\text{MPa})
          \approx -0.075\;\text{K}
\]

So the freezing point is about **–0.08 °C** (≈ –0.1 °C).  

In other words, at 10 kPa water will freeze just a few hundredths of a degree below 0 °C.
